1. Approach and Rationale
   We address the Erdős minimum overlap problem by leveraging Fourier analysis combined with local search. The core idea is to decompose the step function into orthogonal components using a B-spline basis, which explicitly handles the boundary conditions and periodic structure. This decomposition reduces the optimization problem into a constrained and unconstrained phase, allowing us to find structures that minimize overlap at all shifts. The approach avoids direct optimization in high-dimensional space by focusing on time-frequency characteristics of the step function. The main bottleneck addressed is the limited exploration space in local optimizations - we estimate a 7-dimensional optimization space providing sufficient freedom while reducing degeneracy.
